blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Hierarchy and power in British organisations operate on two levels at once. The visible level — titles, reporting lines, compensation bands — is the one newcomers see and study. The invisible level — who is quietly trusted, whose opinion shifts a room, who has the unwritten permission to disagree with the CEO without consequence — is where the real decisions live.

A classic mistake is to treat the two levels as the same. They are not. A junior director may carry more real weight than a senior VP, not because of their title, but because they were at the right dinner ten years ago, or because they are trusted with the kind of difficult truth the CEO cannot hear from anyone else. Nothing in the org chart will tell you this.

At executive level, reading the invisible hierarchy is the single most important political skill in a British company. Decisions that seem inexplicable become obvious once you know who really carries weight, and with whom. And once you see it, you stop wasting energy on people who cannot, in fact, help you — however senior their title sounds.

items.q: According to the text, where do the real decisions live?
options: In the reporting lines and compensation bands
At the level of titles and seniority
In the invisible level of quiet trust and unwritten permission
In the formal org chart studied by newcomers
items.why: "The invisible level… is where the real decisions live."

items.q: Why might a junior director carry more weight than a senior VP?
options: Because the org chart places them above the VP
Because they manage a larger team
Because their compensation band is higher
Because they are trusted with difficult truths the CEO cannot hear elsewhere
items.why: "trusted with the kind of difficult truth the CEO cannot hear from anyone else."

items.q: The phrase "Nothing in the org chart will tell you this" most strongly suggests that…
options: British companies keep their charts secret
real influence is not captured by formal structure
org charts are usually out of date
junior directors should be promoted faster
items.why: Inferência: a fonte da influência é invisível — o organograma não a registra.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Reading who is trusted is a genuine political skill.
Someone's real influence can exceed what their title implies.
Inexplicable decisions often make sense once you know who is trusted.
The most senior title in the room always signals the most power.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo argumenta que o título, sozinho, não determina o poder real.

items.q: What does the closing point about "wasting energy" imply?
options: Titles no longer matter in modern companies
Networking should be avoided at executive level
Effort spent courting the wrong people yields nothing, however senior they are
items.why: Inferência: uma vez que você lê a hierarquia invisível, para de investir em quem não pode, de fato, ajudá-lo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James explicando ao novo executivo quem realmente manda no comitê. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome aboard. Before your first investment committee, let me save you a few painful months. On paper, the CFO chairs that room and signs off on every decision. In practice, the person you need to win over is Diane — a junior director you have probably never heard of.

Here is what the org chart will not tell you. Ten years ago, Diane was the only one willing to tell the previous CEO that a flagship deal was a mistake. She was right, and it was quietly remembered. Since then, when she raises a doubt, the room goes still. Her title has barely moved; her weight in that room is enormous.

So a word of advice. Do not spend your first month flattering the CFO and ignoring Diane. If she is unconvinced, your proposal will die — not loudly, just gently, in a way nobody minutes. Take her to lunch. Ask what she thinks before you present, not after.

None of this is written down anywhere, and no one will explain it to you. But once you can read who is actually trusted, the decisions that used to look baffling will suddenly make perfect sense.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Who does James say the new hire really needs to win over?
options: The CFO, who chairs the committee
items.why: "the person you need to win over is Diane — a junior director."

items.q: Why is Diane so trusted in that room?
options: She once told the previous CEO a flagship deal was a mistake, and was right
She has worked there the longest
She has the most senior title after the CFO
items.why: "the only one willing to tell the previous CEO that a flagship deal was a mistake. She was right."

items.q: What does James mean by a proposal dying "gently, in a way nobody minutes"?
options: It will be rewritten by the committee
It will be formally voted down and recorded
It will be delayed for a few minutes
It will quietly fail without any official rejection on record
items.why: Inferência: 'minute' aqui é registrar em ata — a proposta morre sem rejeição registrada, silenciosamente.

items.q: What is James's underlying advice about seniority and titles?
options: Always defer to the most senior title in the room
Real influence can sit well below the top title, so read it before you act
Titles reliably indicate who holds power
Junior staff should never be consulted first
items.why: Inferência: ele ensina a ler o poder real, que não coincide com o título.

items.q: How would you best describe James's tone toward the new hire?
options: Warm and mentoring, sharing insider knowledge
items.why: Inferência: 'Welcome aboard', 'let me save you a few painful months', 'a word of advice' — postura de mentor.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "On paper she is junior, yet in the boardroom she clearly carries weight." To carry weight means to…
items.why: To carry weight = ter peso, exercer influência real sobre as decisões.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Her ___ says she reports to the CFO, but everyone knows she answers to no one."
items.why: Reporting line = linha de reporte, a quem a pessoa formalmente responde no organograma.

items.q: "He seems to have unwritten permission to challenge the CEO in public." This describes…
options: a promotion he has not yet received
a clause hidden in his contract
a warning he was given verbally
an informal licence that no policy records
items.why: Unwritten permission = permissão tácita: uma licença informal que nenhuma regra registra.

items.q: "Reading the invisible hierarchy is the sharpest political skill at this level." A political skill here is…
options: the ability to navigate power and influence inside an organisation
items.why: Political skill = habilidade política: saber navegar poder e influência dentro da empresa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Their decision looked ___ until I learned who had quietly opposed it."
items.why: Inexplicable = inexplicável: sem explicação aparente, até você conhecer os bastidores.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem quando se fala de poder e influência nos bastidores. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on every committee decision." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Two directors quietly pushed back on the proposal in the corridor." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — muitas vezes de forma discreta, não frontal.

items.q: "Get her on side early, or the plan will quietly die." To get someone on side means to…
items.why: Get someone on side = trazer alguém para o seu lado, conquistar o apoio da pessoa.

items.q: "He tends to hold court at the end of every meeting, and people wait for his verdict." To hold court means to…
options: dominate attention while others defer to you
items.why: Hold court = ser o centro das atenções, com os demais lhe prestando deferência.

items.q: "Flattering the wrong people will not move the needle on your proposal." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir uma diferença perceptível.
